clue.text: When guns are effectively fired in anger, perhaps?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something fired up is set off and agitated, so the letters of anger are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about shooting in a rage, with the guns going off in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Guns fire effectively only when the target is within reach; 'fired' is the anagram signal, while 'perhaps' flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns are effective only when the target lies within their reach, which is the idiom describing the position.

clue.text: In-law embracing diver-cee? That's not quite right

indicators.note: embracing means the first pieces hold another piece within their arms

parts.note: taken as written
an act is a law passed by a parliament
a divorcee, spelt playfully, is somebody's former partner, an ex

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a relative by marriage hugging a divorcee is quite proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver-cee' is a jokey spelling of divorcee, a former spouse; 'embracing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imprecise is not exactly correct, falling slightly short of accuracy.

clue.text: Treatment received by troops losing Turkish capital

indicators.note: losing means the troops word drops one of its letters

parts.note: a regiment is a body of troops

indicators.note: a capital here is the opening letter of the word Turkish

explanation.surface: Medical care is given by soldiers who have lost Ankara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes T, the first letter of Turkish ('capital'), from REGIMENT. 'Turkish capital' looks like Ankara or Istanbul.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of medical care, diet or exercise.

clue.text: Man in the orchestra gives Beethoven's choral symphony

indicators.note: gives signals that the words before it yield up a run of their own letters

explanation.surface: A player in the orchestra performs Beethoven's great choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'maN IN THe'; 'gives' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's last completed symphony, with its choral finale, is No 9.

clue.text: Meet in French bar

parts.note: en is French for in
a counter is a bar in a shop or pub

explanation.surface: An instruction to rendezvous in a French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone, especially by chance, is to come across them.

clue.text: Dishing out for a party

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word dishing are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Serving up food for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, noisy party or celebration.

clue.text: Brush a fur coat

definitions.meaning: an artist's brush made from marten hair
the dark fur of a small Siberian marten, worn as a coat

explanation.definitionFit: Sable names both a fine artist's paintbrush made from marten hair and the prized marten fur itself.

clue.text: Introductory speech, perhaps

definitions.meaning: marking a beginning, as of a term in office
a first address given on taking office, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: An introductory event is a first one; a new president's first address is called by the same word.

clue.text: I'd burst out upset

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the words before it are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone says they burst out in anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to trouble or agitate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Out of range of French explosive device

indicators.note: out of signals the letters of range are knocked out of order

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French explosive lies beyond reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of range' reads as beyond reach, but 'Out of' is the anagram signal, making GRENA.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, an example of an explosive device.

clue.text: It's to do with good breeding

definitions.text: It's to do with good breeding

parts.words: It's to do with good breeding
parts.note: reads like a remark about manners, but means relating to improving hereditary stock

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the science of improving a population's inherited qualities by selective breeding.

clue.text: Wood that is metal to start with

indicators.note: to start with places the metal before the other piece

parts.note: brass is an alloy metal
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece of timber that begins as metal.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassie is an old name for a golf club, the number two wood, once soled with brass.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an old number-two club with a brass sole is one of the woods.

clue.text: The poor may find it accommodating

definitions.text: The poor may find it accommodating

parts.words: The poor may find it accommodating
parts.note: accommodating seems to mean obliging, but means providing lodging, as a charity house does for the needy

explanation.definitionFit: Charitable housing was historically provided for poor or elderly people to live in.

clue.text: Cheese made with some French backing in Goa

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside Goa

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means the French word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: du is French for some

explanation.surface: A cheese produced with a little French help in the Indian state of Goa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' makes UD. Goa is a state on India's west coast; 'made with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild Dutch cheese named after its town of origin.

clue.text: Port one gets in casks

indicators.note: gets in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: tuns are large casks for wine or beer
I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A harbour where someone fills barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is a Mediterranean port and capital of Tunisia.

clue.text: Propose a broadcast on the first of August-a serial drama

indicators.note: broadcast, scattered abroad, signals the letters of the words before it are spread into a new order
the first of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone suggests airing a serialised television drama starting in August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges PROPOSE A as SOAPOPER; 'the first of' gives A from August.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running domestic television serial is the classic example of the genre named after detergent sponsors.

clue.text: Fair distribution of beer to all

indicators.note: distribution of means the letters of the phrase are handed out in a new order

explanation.surface: Fairly sharing beer around everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of middling or passable means acceptable enough, a synonym.

clue.text: One fond of girls put damsel in a turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil signals the letters of the words before it are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: A womaniser puts a young woman into a state of upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who enjoys and seeks the company of women is called by this phrase.

clue.text: Some French married, but didn't expect to be happy

parts.note: des is French for some
paired means joined as a couple, married

explanation.surface: Some French couple wed while having no hope of happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To have given up all hope is to have no expectation of happiness.

clue.text: Hell for a Welshman at his mother's side

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, hell
Taff is a slang nickname for a Welshman

explanation.surface: Hell for a Welshman alongside his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: TAFF is British slang for a Welshman, from the River Taff in Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female line, from the spinning staff associated with women.

clue.text: Please pay in full

definitions.meaning: to settle a debt or claim completely

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to content a person and to discharge a debt completely.

clue.text: Don't take time off

definitions.meaning: to abandon or not take something with you
a holiday or period away from work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to go without taking something and a period of permitted absence from work.

clue.text: Yet a cricketer is not out to improve his

definitions.text: Yet a cricketer is not out to improve his

parts.words: Yet a cricketer is not out to improve his
parts.note: a batsman finishing an innings not out raises his runs-per-dismissal figure, since no dismissal is counted

explanation.walkthrough: A not-out innings adds runs without adding a dismissal, so the batting figure goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman's runs divided by dismissals is the statistic that rises when he is not out.

clue.text: Could be set near China, for example

indicators.note: could be signals the letters of the words after it might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A remark that something might be placed near China.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the Orient, so it is an example of a country described by this adjective.

clue.text: Start to fight

parts.note: to set off is to start; set is a start word as in ready, steady
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument.

clue.text: Port of fine quality

definitions.meaning: a town and port on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent
the gauzy, thin quality of a fabric

explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is a port in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Kent port and the transparency or thinness of a fine fabric.

clue.text: People aren't wanted on this board

definitions.text: People aren't wanted on this board

parts.words: People aren't wanted on this board
parts.note: board seems a committee, but is a plank; being on it means being unwanted, especially unmarried

explanation.definitionFit: Being left on this plank means being passed over, as an unmarried person once was.

clue.text: How bread's gone up!

parts.note: sounds like a grumble about prices, but describes dough that has proved

explanation.definitionFit: Dough that has proved has expanded upwards, the past participle of the verb for ascending.

clue.text: Possibly a Surete stiff!

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the words after it may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Perhaps a corpse found by the French police.
explanation.walkthrough: The Surete is the French detective police; 'stiff' looks like a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and formal in manner, as is a stiff person.

clue.text: Seem upset about flag signal

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round another piece
upset means the letters of the word seem are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: to flag is to droop or sag

explanation.surface: Looking upset about a signal sent by flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives MESE; 'flag' looks like a banner for signalling, but here it is the verb to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a communication sent from one party to another.

clue.text: Rugby player is crafty one of pair

parts.note: fly is British slang for cunning or crafty
each of two equal parts is a half

explanation.surface: A rugby player is cunning and forms one of a duo.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY is British slang for sharp or cunning. The half-backs in rugby are a pair: the fly-half and the scrum-half.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the fly-half is the back who directs play, partnering the scrum-half.

clue.text: Girl with enthusiasm for the cloth

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name
keen expresses eagerness or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A young woman is eager for the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally from Nanjing.
